facts.fact: A man in a grey cloak from the queen's household approached Muthu the winter Asha died and asked for a monthly letter 'to keep the warden safe'. Muthu's mother is alive and writes to him on the ninth-day post, as F217 says.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Muthu confess how the letters began.

facts.fact: The thick grey packet Devan locked away holds Muthu's month-report on two leaves plus the household's order slip ('Say nothing, and your wife is kept') in a clerk's round hand. Ittan read the slip and handed it back, and Muthu enclosed it with his own letter.
facts.why: reconciles the packet Muthu carried into Ittan's cell (beat 2) with the locked packet Devan opens (beat 3, ch 31 continuity).

facts.fact: Muthu keeps a small brass post-key on a cord at his belt for the gate's post chest; Devan takes it so all post passes through Devan's hand.
facts.why: the beat has Devan 'take the post-key'.

facts.fact: Muthu's letters to the household never mention where Devan lays his sword, yet Vellan knew (F214/F220), which points to an informant who has been in the warden's chamber. Neela and Devan conclude it is not Muthu. This is clue C11.
facts.why: plants C11 and the reader question out.

facts.fact: The raid on the Resin House goes in on the dark of the moon, with Devan leading the ridge party and Muthu holding Kettamala with Rema inside the walls.
facts.why: the beat has Devan naming Muthu to hold Kettamala during the raid; the timing is a small added detail.
